article.headline: Lakers open revamped roster against Kings with Kessler in focus
article.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers begin their preseason Monday against the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center, with new center Walker Kessler and young wings Cameron Carr and Adou Thiero getting significant playing time.
article.body:
Los Angeles brought in seven new players this offseason to rebuild its roster depth, making Monday's preseason opener against Sacramento a chance to see how the pieces fit together. The Lakers signed Williams and Thybulle for their defensive prowess and three-point shooting, while Sexton will anchor the bench as a scoring option. Kessler, who the team acquired for two unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps, will play limited minutes but offers the most intrigue as he pairs with stars Dončić and Reaves.

Monday's game matters because preseason provides the first look at how these acquisitions blend on the court. Star players like Dončić and Reaves will see limited minutes, typical for exhibition games, allowing the roster's new wing prospects and younger players to showcase their abilities. Carr and Thiero impressed during the 2026 NBA Summer League, averaging 18 and 15.4 points per game respectively, and both will get significant looks.

The Lakers are banking on their hybrid wings to defend and stretch the floor next to Dončić. The team also acquired Kessler, Looney, Mamukelashvili, Grimes, and Sexton, along with Williams and Thybulle, creating a nearly complete roster overhaul from the offseason. Kessler's rim protection and chemistry with the guards will be watched closely despite his expected limited playing time.

article.headline: Daniil Medvedev disqualified for hitting spectator during China Open semi-final against Djokovic
article.summary: Daniil Medvedev was defaulted from his China Open semi-final match against Novak Djokovic on Monday after striking a spectator with a ball.
article.body: The incident occurred while Novak Djokovic was serving for a spot in the final, when Medvedev reacted to a ball ricocheting off the back of the court by swiping it into the stands. The ball struck a spectator directly in the face, leading to the disqualification of the Russian player just a few minutes later. Under tennis regulations, players are strictly barred from hitting a ball in a dangerous or reckless manner, or with negligent disregard for the consequences regarding the safety of officials, ball kids, and spectators. While Medvedev maintains that he is a calm individual off the court and that his tennis-related aggression fades quickly once he departs the venue, this disqualification marks the end of his run at the China Open. The BBC reports that the decision was deemed necessary given the nature of the action. Medvedev has a history of on-court outbursts, previously facing fines at the 2019 US Open for his treatment of a ball person and making offensive gestures toward fans. In a 2017 Wimbledon match, he also caused controversy by sprinkling coins at the feet of umpire Mariana Alves during a heated exchange. Despite his tendency for explosive behavior during matches, Medvedev remains a popular figure with the media for his humorous and reflective interviews after play concludes. His frustration often manifests as irritation directed toward umpires and officials, sometimes resulting in game penalties throughout his career as a junior and professional athlete.

article.headline: Coco Gauff Routs Teenager in Beijing After Racist Abuse Online Backlash
article.summary: Coco Gauff reached the China Open fourth round with a 7-5, 6-1 win following a controversial replayed point.
article.body: Coco Gauff faced an insane volume of racist direct messages and social media comments immediately following her 7-5, 6-1 victory over 16-year-old Sun Xinran in Beijing. The 22-year-old American champion addressed the vitriol directly on X, stating that viewers could disagree with the match events without resorting to racism while clarifying she is neither a cheater nor a thief. The online backlash followed a pivotal moment in the first set when Gauff stopped play at 4-5 to report a flickering advertising board that she believed acted as a hindrance. Following a video review, the umpire permitted the point to be replayed, which Gauff subsequently won to hold serve and eventually dominate the remaining sets. According to BBC and TODAY.com, rules allow players to request such reviews if they believe a distraction has interfered with play. Gauff confirmed she apologized to Sun at the net, describing the teenager as an incredible talent and noting that Sun understood the situation was beyond anyone's control. The issue of online harassment remains a significant concern for the sport, as the WTA and World Tennis reported that female players were subjected to 12,000 abusive posts throughout 2025. This figure marks an increase from 8,000 recorded in the previous year. In response to the growing trend, the WTA has implemented an AI-powered system designed to monitor and address such content directed at players and officials. Gauff is now slated to compete in the tournament's last 16 phase.

article.headline: Budget 2027 Ramps Up Help To Buy To €35k For First-Time Buyers
article.summary: Government leaders have finalized Budget 2027, featuring a €5,000 tax rebate increase, a €10 weekly pension hike, and adjustments to inheritance thresholds.
article.body:
First-time buyers will see their Help to Buy tax rebate rise by €5,000 to a total of €35,000 as part of the newly finalized financial package. This specific adjustment comes as government coalition leaders concluded crunch talks on Monday night to shift the focus toward workers, following a previous cycle that officials acknowledged left households worse off.

For most citizens, the budget brings immediate changes to social welfare and income tax thresholds. The State pension is set to rise by €10 per week, a figure that also applies to all other core social welfare payments. Additionally, the entry point for the 40% higher rate of income tax will shift from €44,000 to €46,500, a move that is €500 higher than what was initially expected by market analysts and observers.

Beyond basic income adjustments, the government has introduced a new permanent disability payment of €500. Families will receive an additional €6 per week in child support payments, though the standard Children’s Allowance remains unchanged. Those relying on social welfare will also receive a fuel allowance increase of €5 and the customary Christmas bonus. Regarding capital acquisitions, inheritance tax thresholds are rising across all categories, with the parent-to-child limit climbing by €20,000 to reach €420,000.

While the budget aims to alleviate cost-of-living pressures, it notably excludes energy credits, which will not be part of the 2027 package. Finance ministers Jack Chambers and Simon Harris are scheduled to present the formal details to Dáil Éireann on Tuesday afternoon to confirm the public spending and taxation strategy for the coming year.

article.headline: British Airways jet plunges 28,000 feet before emergency landing at Heathrow
article.summary: A Chicago-bound flight returned to London Heathrow on Monday after a technical issue forced a rapid descent over Ireland.
article.body:
Oxygen masks dangled from the cabin ceiling as a Boeing 777-200ER descended from its cruising altitude to below 10,000 feet in a matter of minutes. The sudden drop occurred roughly an hour into the transatlantic journey, prompting pilots to issue a 7700 emergency squawk and abort the flight to Chicago’s O’Hare airport.

This incident highlights the standard emergency protocols required when an aircraft encounters unexpected technical difficulties at high altitude. The immediate descent ensures that cabin pressure is stabilized, protecting the safety of those on board, while the subsequent return to a major hub like Heathrow allows for a controlled resolution of the mechanical alert.

According to The Guardian and the Daily Star, the flight, identified as BA295, departed London Heathrow on Monday. While passengers reported uncertainty as the masks deployed, they noted that the descent itself did not feel overly rapid and praised the crew for their handling of the situation. After declaring the emergency over Ireland, the pilots spent several hours flying in a holding pattern over the Bristol Channel. This maneuver was necessary to burn off sufficient fuel to meet weight requirements for a safe landing. The aircraft eventually landed back at Heathrow just after 5pm.

British Airways confirmed that the aircraft landed safely and that customers disembarked normally. The airline is now coordinating efforts to assist passengers in rescheduling their travel plans to their intended destinations.
